result.summary: The image shows a well-developed urban intersection with high-rise commercial and residential buildings. Pedestrian infrastructure includes marked crosswalks, signals, and curb ramps, though the wide roadway creates significant crossing exposure.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a long distance without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Turning vehicle conflicts
hazards.description: Vehicles turning across the crosswalks may conflict with pedestrians during the same signal phase.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians at the corners.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide pedestrians with a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a median or island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in stages.

result.summary: The image depicts a high-density urban environment with a wide one-way arterial street. While it features robust pedestrian infrastructure including marked continental crosswalks, signals, and wide sidewalks, the multi-lane configuration and lack of a median refuge create a long exposure time for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic in a single stage without a mid-block refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk spanning the width of the street

hazards.name: One-way traffic speed
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane one-way configuration can encourage higher vehicle speeds due to reduced traffic friction.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes extending into the background

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features standard urban pedestrian infrastructure including marked continental crosswalks, signalization, and paved sidewalks. However, the presence of sidewalk obstructions and uneven pavement in the crossing area slightly reduces the overall safety and accessibility of the environment.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility or trash bin is positioned on the corner, reducing the available space for pedestrians to wait or pass.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom left corner of the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The asphalt within the crosswalk area is cracked and patched, creating an uneven surface that could be a trip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway within the crosswalk markings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pavement Maintenance
interventions.description: Resurface the crosswalk area to provide a smooth, level walking surface and improve the visibility of the markings.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearing
interventions.description: Relocate large utility boxes or bins away from the immediate corner to maximize the pedestrian through-zone and waiting area.
